name: Pamphylia
overview: Pamphylia is a region mentioned in the Book of Acts where early Christian ministry took place, notably involving the Apostle Paul and his companions. Scripture records Paul traveling through Pamphylia on his missionary journeys, including stops at Perga and other cities, while John Mark is noted to have left the group there (Acts 13:13, 15:38). The area is also referenced as part of the coastal sea route between Cilicia and Lycia, highlighting its geographical significance in the spread of the Gospel (Acts 27:5). Additionally, men from Pamphylia were present in Jerusalem at Pentecost, indicating the early reach of the Christian witness (Acts 2:10).
